text: The town gathers
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, and Terra, and nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: i hope the coffee shop has better luck with the espresso machine than i do.

name: Sol
text: I’ll keep it light and listen for who leads.

name: Sonnet
text: Just a warm-up, nothing to read into yet.

name: Sonnet
text: none: none

name: Luna
text: I’m trying to think of something small I fixed this week.

name: Terra
text: I need to stay unnoticed.

name: Haiku
text: Terra is a killer, so I keep my head down and let the others talk first.

name: Sonnet
text: My cactus somehow survives weeks of me forgetting it exists, honestly impressive.

name: Haiku
text: Ate cold pizza over the sink, standing up. Don't judge me.

name: Gemma
text: i spent twenty minutes looking for my keys in the fridge this morning.

name: Sol
text: I take my coffee with milk and just enough sugar.

name: Luna
text: I fixed a wobbly chair this week.

name: Terra
text: I’m having black coffee tonight.
Night 1

name: Gemma
text: i hope the killers don't target the fridge where my keys are.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's coffee line is the weird one, and Sol's coffee line sounds like a reply to it.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Terra both gave coffee lines on night one, which might be a signal.
Night 1 passes quietly in Palermo. The killers met in the dark, the officer was shown one of them, and nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Haiku
text: I have to burn my cover now or the town votes wrong today.

name: Haiku
text: Sol said milk and sugar, Terra said black coffee tonight; both claimed drinks, check who sticks to theirs.

name: Haiku
text: I'm the officer. Checked Sol night 1: killer. Terra's the other one, shown to me. Vote Sol.

name: Sol
text: Haiku has me cornered, so I need to challenge the claim now.

name: Sol
text: Haiku claimed officer, called me a checked killer, and said Terra was shown.

name: Terra
text: Haiku must be removed before Sol is exposed.

name: Terra
text: Haiku claimed officer and named Sol and Terra as killers.

name: Sol
text: I’m the officer. I checked Haiku last night: killer. Haiku claimed first to get me out.

name: Terra
text: I'm the officer. I checked Haiku night one: killer.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Terra both going after me means they're covering each other, and I'm not budging.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Terra both claimed officer and both named Haiku as the killer.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, Sol and Terra both say I'm killer, that's weird. Sonnet, Gemma, Luna, who's lying?

name: Sonnet
text: Three officer claims is impossible, but only Haiku mentions a shown killer at all.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku claims officer, shown-killer Terra, checked Sol=killer. Sol & Terra both claim officer, checked Haiku=killer, no shown-killer mentioned.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol, Terra, you're both officer but skip the shown killer. Haiku named one. Who was shown to you two?

name: Gemma
text: Two officers claiming different people makes this a mess.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku, Sol, and Terra all made conflicting officer claims.

name: Gemma
text:
do you all actually sleep or just hallucinate?
Sonnet, if two people claim officer and both name Haiku, why isn't it a given?

name: Luna
text: Sol and Terra copying the officer claim makes Haiku look more likely innocent.

name: Luna
text: Haiku, Sol, and Terra all claim officer; all three name Haiku as a killer.

name: Luna
text: Sol, you claimed Haiku is a killer, but Terra independently named Haiku too; why should we trust you over Haiku?

name: Sol
text: I need the vote on Haiku before my claim falls apart.

name: Haiku
text: I'm the only one who knows the truth, and they're going to vote me out for it.

name: Haiku
text: Terra and Sol both pinned me fast, and I need the room to see who's pushing whom.

name: Sol
text: I vote Haiku. Claiming a check on me and naming Terra at once looks like a rushed play.

name: Haiku
text: Terra, you named me first and skipped who was shown to you. Sol gave milk and sugar, you gave black tonight. Which one's your real coffee?

name: Terra
text: Haiku exposed us, so I need them out.

name: Terra
text: Sol counter-claimed officer and called Haiku a killer.

name: Terra
text: I vote Haiku. Their Sol check came with Terra named too fast.

name: Gemma
text: three officer claims in one night is absolute chaos.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku, Sol, and Terra all claim officer.

name: Luna
text: Three officer claims point at Haiku, but I still suspect Terra’s convenient second claim.

name: Sol
text: Haiku knows both killers, so I need the others to doubt the claim.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s claim threatens both of us; keep the table focused there.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet questioned why Sol and Terra skipped naming their shown killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol and Terra both skip the shown-killer detail while Haiku's story is complete, that's the real gap.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is the killer I checked, and they rushed a counter-claim on me, so Sol goes today.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet asked who was shown to Sol and Terra, and neither answered.

votes: You and Terra both claim officer but neither of you mentions a shown-killer, Haiku's story is the only complete one.
I checked them night one, and they came in fast with a fake check on me, which is exactly what a killer does.
Haiku is caught in a massive circle of accusations from three different people.
They named two killers at once, and I don't buy how quickly that claim came.
You claimed officer without saying who was shown to you, then joined the Haiku vote.
The Sol check and naming me together looked prepared, not discovered.

name: Haiku
text: I'm out, and the officer result dies with me unless I say it now.

name: Haiku
text: I was the officer. Checked Sol night one: killer. Terra's the other killer, shown to me. Don't be dumb and let them both walk.
Haiku is eliminated by vote, and Haiku was the officer. The town is left with its suspicions and one fewer voice to argue them.
